title: ReFocusEraser: Refocusing for Small Object Removal with Robust Context-Shadow Repair
claim: Small distant objects lose detail when compressed by the encoder, but enlarging them through zoom before inpainting preserves detail and improves results.
layout: 3 columns by 3 rows of zoom levels, left-to-right, with zoomed crop insets
description: On the left, an input image with a tiny person on a sports field is shown with a red zoom-in crop and a yellow ground-truth (GT) crop. Below it is a black mask with a small white silhouette. A camera icon labeled 'Camera Control' leads through a brace to three rows at 1×, 2× and 3× focal length (FL). Column (a) shows the input at each zoom, with a green dashed box marking the zoomed region. Column (b) shows the VAE reconstruction, with red inset crops that become sharper as zoom increases. Column (c) shows the inpainting result, with yellow dashed mask boxes and yellow inset crops. The 1× inpaint is blurry and smeared, and the 3× result looks cleaner. Green dashed arrows link (a) to (b). The eye goes first to the photo grid and its colored insets.
caption: Illustration of camera-adaptive refocus. Far-field regions are zoomed in near-field views, enlarging small masked objects and preserving details during inpainting. ‘FL’ is focal length.
abstract: Existing diffusion-based object removal and inpainting methods often fail to recover the fine structural and textural details of small objects. This is primarily due to the VAE encoder’s downsampling, which inevitably compresses small masked regions and causes significant detail loss, while the decoder’s upsampling alone cannot fully restore the lost fine details. However, the adverse effects of this fixed compression can be mitigated by enlarging the perspective of these regions. To this end, we propose ReFocusEraser, a two-stage framework for small object removal that combines camera-adaptive zoom-in inpainting with robust context- and shadow-aware repair. In Stage I, a camera-adaptive refocus mechanism magnifies masked regions, and a LoRA-tuned diffusion model ensures precise semantic alignment for accurate reconstruction. However, reintegrating these magnified inpainted regions into the original image introduces challenges due to VAE asymmetry, such as color shifts and seams. Stage II addresses these issues by fine-tuning an additional decoder to create a seam- and shadow-aware module that eliminates residual artifacts while preserving background consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed RefocusEraser achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods across benchmark datasets. Related code and data are available at https://github.com/ProAirVerse/ReFocusEraser.git.
